c2787.summary: Tyagaraja invites Rama to come to his house, describing how he would serve him and forget all his troubles.
m: Come, come to our house, valiant and tender hero of the Raghus — I bow to you.
Come, son of Dasharatha, take me as your own — I can bear it no longer, Rama.
My wishes unfulfilled, O lotus-eyed one, looking only down your path,
I grew weary; protector of good people, you went off on a journey — Lord, at least today (come).
Rising at dawn, you would counsel me with good thoughts and protect me; your lovely
face I would behold, standing near you, worshipping you always.
Knowing that you are my refuge, come quickly in compassion to protect me;
I will forget all the troubles I have been caught in — O fortune of Sri Tyagaraja.

c1281.summary: Why don't you answer me, Rama? Did I worship some seducer or thief?
m: Why don't you answer me, O delight of my heart?
Did I worship a seducer or a thief, O dweller in Saketa?
You who came from afar and settled in the lotus of my heart,
knowing the way, and rejoiced — O one praised by Tyagaraja.

c2870.summary: Who can charm Rama with beautiful music — perfect rhythm, pure svara, true devotion and the nine rasas? Is Tyagaraja capable of it?
m: Who is the hero who can charm you, keeping beautiful time with the mridanga,
with true words that hold the essence of the Vedas, and with purity of svara,
with pauses and rests, true devotion and detachment, with the nine rasas, sweet as grape juice,
worshipping you with compositions — is such skill within Tyagaraja's reach, Sri Rama?

c2227.summary: Tyagaraja protests that he never claimed to be Rama's devotee out of greed, and that Rama's feet are his only refuge.
m: Did I, out of greed, falsely claim on earth to be your servant, O delight of the wise?
Did I take crooked paths, begging thoughtless men? Protect me.
In great joy or sorrow, I have suffered among my peers;
whether you plunge me in milk or in water, your feet alone are my refuge, O one praised by Tyagaraja.

c2655.summary: Tyagaraja trusts Rama's lotus feet, recalling how Rama broke Shiva's bow, freed Ahalya, and helped Sugriva.
m: I have trusted completely in your lotus feet,
you who broke Shiva's bow to crush the pride of kings;
who ended the anguish of Ahalya, who, cursed long ago in anger by the sage, day after day
lay as a stone, unable to bear her torment;
lotus-eyed one, who could not bear the suffering Indra's son (Vali) caused, and as fear grew in the mind of the Sun's son (Sugriva),
kicked away the huge dark skeleton of Dundubhi with your toe;
praised by the lord of Parvati, beloved of the Earth's daughter, refuge of Tyagaraja,
praised by Rudra, protector of Brahmins, life of the sages — always (I trust your feet).

c2575.summary: Tyagaraja reminds Rama of the promise he once made — to protect him well — and asks him not to break it.
m: Don't break today the word you gave long ago, my father, Sri Rama.
'I will protect well the one who has not left me since he was a child' — (so you said);
'trouble aimed at his head will only take his turban; one who trusts me as at the bridge will not be caught in a snare';
'I will lift him onto the ocean of devotion on this earth' — you vowed this solemnly, O one worshipped by Tyagaraja.

c1284.summary: How wonderful are the Lord's illusions — he does everything and says 'not I', as he taught Arjuna in the Gita.
m: How wonderful are your illusions! Can even Brahma praise them fully?
Doing all this mischief, and then saying 'it is not I'!
That day, to destroy the Kauravas, seeing Arjuna dread the sin,
did you not protect him well, saying 'the fruit of sin is neither yours nor his'? O one praised by Tyagaraja.

c2383.summary: What use is it to describe the Lord's glories to the people of the Kali age who wear devotion only as a disguise?
m: Has it not been said: what use is it to tell your glories to the people of the Kali age?
It is like expecting fine bullocks on earth to know the taste of delicacies.
For wives and children, for wealth, for village and fame, for great status,
to those who keep wearing the guise of devotees — O saving name, worshipped by Sri Tyagaraja.

c2748.summary: A lover's complaint to Rama: I longed for you and grew weary, yet you show no compassion.
m: Rama, delightful one, of lovely name, terror to the enemies of the good, dweller in Saketa.
Lotus-eyed one, I loved you and grew weary; there is no compassion in your heart — what use is my sulking?
My heart is infatuated with you alone, yet you don't take our hand affectionately and protect us.
Though I longed and longed to serve you, your path went another way — perhaps it is what Brahma wrote.
I made a lovely bed; without delighting in it, you make me a public spectacle.
Day after day I trust that you are my refuge; what merit do you find in counting my highs and lows?
Compassion must arise in you, and you must protect me, moon-faced one, giver of boons to Tyagaraja.

c2568.summary: Tyagaraja asks Rama to accompany and guard him on all sides — in front, behind and on either side.
m: Come with me in front, behind and on either side, O slayer of Mura and Khara — come.
Where could one find beauty like yours? Delight of the Raghus, come quickly.
Moon to the ocean of the blazing Solar race, come bearing the Kodanda bow.
Come with Saumitri, who serves at your side, O one of valour, come.
O protector of the elephant, O prince, abode of Om, come.
Dear to devotees, protect me well, praised by Tyagaraja, come.

c1064.summary: Why this hesitation in protecting me, Rama?
m: Why this hesitation, lotus-eyed one, in protecting me?
Does it seem to you that I don't understand hints and that I beg others? O you whose radiance outshines ten thousand suns, protect me now.
Some say you bear every title for releasing hosts of true devotees from sin;
you tease me — you who crowned the best of the forest-dwellers (Sugriva), worshipped by Tyagaraja.

c1447.summary: Where is your dwelling place, Lord? In the goddesses, the elements, the worlds, or the gods?
m: Where is your dwelling place? Even searching, I cannot find it.
Is it in the forms of Sita, Gauri and Sarasvati, Govinda?
Is it in the earth, moon, sun, wind and sky? In the countless worlds?
Or in Shiva, Madhava, Brahma and the rest — O giver of good, worshipped by Tyagaraja's hands?

c2882.summary: Tyagaraja's joy at seeing the divine form of Tripurasundari of Tiruvottiyur at her Friday worship.
m: O beautiful one, I have been blessed to see your divine form, Mother.
Is it the power of your gentle glance, or the fruit of my past worship, O Tripura?
Hearing of the beauty of you who dwell in noble Adipura on earth, the wise
Brahma and the gods gather together, melting, wondering 'will we get to see the Friday worship?' —
while in heaven their minds are restless with longing, O remover of the sorrows of the humble, Tripura,
I will praise you before the assembly as the protector of the humble in Kali, O one of graceful virtues,
ocean of compassion, who is your equal, Mother? While I waited, wondering if my weary mind would be soothed,
the celestial women serve you in rows, amid a joyful bustle, on the lovely Friday, Tripura —
my mother who bore me, my life is fulfilled today, Mother, now — like
money to the very poor, a feast for the eyes, O lotus-eyed one, like water to withering crops,
giver of good, sister of Vishnu, delight of Sri Tyagaraja's heart, Gauri.

c1287.summary: A daru from Tyagaraja's opera Prahlada Bhakti Vijayam, describing the doorkeeper Vasudeva making his grand, swaggering entrance.
m: Look at him who has come out, (named) Vasudeva!
Worshipped by Indra and the gods, holding the lotus-eyed Lord in his mind,
wearing fine silk dhotis, with sacred powder on his forehead,
coming out in procession into this assembly, holding a golden staff again and again,
twirling his moustache again and again, puffed up that he is handsome as Manmatha,
leaping and stepping, swaggering, speaking proudly, laughing loudly,
dancing exceedingly well, beseeching the purifier of the fallen,
singing in ragas, talas and rhythms, praising the one praised by Tyagaraja.

c2834.summary: Come and worship Sri Ganapati, who dances in many rhythms with Hari's feet in his heart.
m: Come and serve Sri Ganapati, O people who seek refuge,
who, receiving fine worship from Brahma, the lord of speech, set out, bowing well,
having eaten jackfruit, coconut, rose-apple and other fruits, setting his feet heavily on the earth
with a jingling sound, and holding Hari's feet in the lotus of his heart,
humbly, praised by Tyagaraja, he set out, dancing in various rhythms.

c2341.summary: The meaning of the Gita and the bliss of music come together in one place: Hanuman, who holds Rama's feet.
m: The meaning of the Gita and the bliss of music — see them together in one place, O mind.
Hanuman, son of the Wind, who holds the lotus feet of Sita's Lord, knows them well.
He knows the secrets of the rites and creeds of Hari, Hara, the Sun, Kala and the rest;
he, the noble monkey, praised by Shiva, granter of boons to noble Tyagaraja — he is truly happy.

c2584.summary: Why such delay in protecting me? Rama knows a parent's love — he raised children himself.
m: Why such delay in protecting me? Tell me, what is my fault?
Since childhood I longed for your friendship — did you not think of me, Sri Rama?
Were you not born well among brothers who are your true servants?
Protector of the elephant king, did you not see and raise sons? (You know a parent's love) — praised by Tyagaraja.

c1704.summary: A string of praises for Rama, the smiling-faced charmer of the heart, worshipped with understanding.
m: (I worship) the smiling-faced one, the charmer of my heart, the valiant ruler of the world, beloved of Janaki,
the God of gods, the divinely beautiful, Sri Vasudeva, Sita's Raghava,
treasury of true knowledge, whose eyes are moon and sun, a sun that dispels the darkness of ignorance,
of pure form, remover of all sins, the great one who graciously grants dharma and the other aims up to liberation,
praised by Sri Tyagaraja — whom I worship again and again with understanding.

c6029.summary: A prayer to Ganapati enshrined at Vatapi. Dikshitar describes his iconography and his place in the Muladhara chakra, and signs with 'Guruguha' and the raga's name.
m: I worship Ganapati of Vatapi, the elephant-faced giver of boons,
whose feet are served by the bhutas and others, who sustains the world of the elements, free of attachment, praised by yogis, cause of the universe, remover of obstacles;
worshipped long ago by Agastya, the great sage born of a pot, who dwells at the centre of the triangle,
worshipped by Vishnu and the other chief gods, who resides in the Muladhara,
the essence of the four levels of speech beginning with Para, the curved-trunked one whose form is Om,
who always wears the crescent moon on his forehead, who holds sugarcane in his left hand,
who holds the noose and citron fruit in his lotus hands, far from all impurity, of vast form,
whose form delights Shiva, Guruguha and others — Heramba, adorned by Hamsadhwani.

c3150.summary: Dikshitar declares himself a devotee of Ganapati, consort of Vallabha, giver of all desires.
m: I am the devotee of the consort of Vallabha, giver of all one desires, who rides the noble mouse,
whose feet are soft as tender leaves, who holds the noose and goad, who wears garlands of jasmine and champaka, adorned with jewels,
who brought about Valli's marriage, worshipped by Guruguha, praised by Kali, Kalamalini and lotus-eyed Lakshmi.

c3577.summary: Dikshitar's first composition: a prayer to Mahaganapati of Tiruvarur, describing his form and attributes.
m: May Sri Mahaganapati protect me — Siddhi Vinayaka, the elephant-faced,
praised by Vishnu, Brahma and Indra, dwelling on the banks of the Kamalalaya tank, with tender leaf-like hands and feet, elder brother of Guruguha, son of Shiva;
king of obstacles who draws gold, lotus-footed, wearing white garments,
with the moon on his forehead, praised by men and others, big-bellied, holding the lily, his own tusk, noose, goad and modaka,
radiant, the boat across the ocean of worldly life, blissful in nature as Mula Prakriti,
with a body radiant as a thousand suns, praised by poets, who rides the mouse,
bowed to by hosts of gods, the abode of imperishable liberation.

c5774.summary: Dikshitar meditates on Mahaganapati, son of Shiva, lover of poetry, drama and modakas.
m: I meditate in my mind on Mahaganapati, worshipped by Vasishtha, Vamadeva and others,
son of Mahadeva, praised by Guruguha, radiant as ten million Manmathas, serene,
who loves great poems and dramas, who rides the mouse and is fond of modakas.

c5716.summary: Salutations to the elephant-faced Mahaganapati on his throne, holding his many weapons in his lotus hands.
m: Salutations to you, elephant-faced one, seated on a throne in a golden pavilion,
the great lord of the ganas, worshipped by Shiva who wears an elephant hide, of that very form, who blesses all devotees, whose form is embraced by Maya,
whose lotus hands hold the lotus, lily, noose, conch, discus, sugarcane bow, ears of paddy, mace, his own
tusk, the citron and a jewelled pot — to him whose feet
are lotuses, the pure one, cause of the creation, sustenance and dissolution of the universe, abode of compassion,
a sun to the lotus face of the Himalaya's daughter, the good-minded one,
of noble splendour equal to Guruguha, son of Uma's lord — to the radiant one.

c5624.summary: A prayer to Akhilandeshvari of Tiruvanaikaval, goddess of all the universes, delighting in music.
m: O Akhilandeshvari, protect me, expert in the tradition of the Agamas,
eternal soul of all worlds, spotless, pure, dark-hued, embodiment of all arts,
worshipped by Lambodara and Guruguha, shining with long tresses, smiling one,
worshipped by the goddess of speech, giver of boons, praised by the king of mountains, Sharada,
honoured by Indra, praised by Janardana, praised in the raga Jujavanti,
delighting in the sounds of the jalli, maddala and jhar-jhara drums, giver of knowledge.

c5739.summary: The first of Dikshitar's Kamalamba Navavarna kritis, on the goddess of Tiruvarur and the outermost enclosure of the Sri Chakra.
m: May Kamalamba protect me, who dwells in Kamalanagara, the lotus of the heart,
lotus-faced one worshipped by the gods, beloved companion of the beautiful-minded one, joyful in the bliss of knowledge, parrot in the cage of the sacred syllable,
ruler of the chakras beginning with Tripura, mistress of the siddhis beginning with Anima, eternal Kameshvari,
presiding over the Trailokya Mohana chakra, the outer square of the Sri Chakra, (attended by) the Prakata yoginis,
slayer of Mahishasura and the other enemies of the gods, known through the Vedas and Puranas,
ruler of Tripura, mother of Guruguha, delight of Shiva who destroyed the three cities,
sister of Vishnu, slender-waisted, Tripurasundari, great goddess.

c5740.summary: A Navavarna kriti on Kamalamba of Tiruvarur and the Sarvashaparipuraka chakra (the second enclosure of the Sri Chakra).
m: Worship Kamalamba, O mind; give up the works of imagined illusion —
whose sides are served by Lakshmi and Sarasvati, whose neck surpasses the conch, to whom gods bow, dwelling in Kamalapura, of gentle speech, lovely teeth and lotus face;
ruler of the Sarvashaparipuraka chakra (fulfiller of all desires), beloved of Parama Shiva,
the Gupta yogini worshipped by Durvasa, destroyer of sorrow, the swan,
giver of the bliss of liberation, eternally auspicious, Katyayani,
Sharvani, whose braid outshines the bees, mother of the true guru Guruguha, untainted,
destroyer of the proud Bhandasura, delighted by Kamakarshini and the other shaktis,
whose form is pure consciousness beyond attributes, whose form is the principles beginning with earth.
